subject: Private deployment: network-sanitation, access gating, and sprint action list
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@healthmate.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding — network sanity checks before Private deployment

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for yesterday's intro call. We're excited to move HealthMate onto Redwood Private for inference workloads. Before we kick off a short engineering sprint next week, our infra team asked for a concise checklist of the network and access prerequisites we should complete so the handoff isn't blocked.

Top asks from our side:
- Network diagram (VPC/subnets, peering, required routes).
- Exact egress ports and FQDNs we need to allow for telemetry, model pulls, & runtime (including the token service).
- KMS key access pattern (who needs decrypt/encrypt and how to rotate).
- Service account patterns and whether Redwood needs IAM roles or service principal impersonation.
- Expected MTU/NIC settings for on-prem edge appliances (we run 9000 by default).

Can you send a short, prioritized checklist and a proposed timeline? We're aiming for a 2-week validation window.

Best,
Sara
Ops Lead, HealthMate

--
[sent from mobile]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@healthmate.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding — network sanity checks before Private deployment

Sara — thanks, and welcome aboard. Attached is a concise validation checklist and a first-pass network armature diagram (see attachments). High level we recommend we split the work into two parallel tracks: 1) Network & routing readiness, 2) Access, KMS and telemetry.

I've summarized the immediate, high-priority items below (we'll expand in the doc):

1) Network basics (must-have before we run connectivity tests)
   - VPC/subnet CIDR blocks and an IP plan for Redwood runtime nodes (avoid overlap; provide a /22 per runtime cluster).
   - Ensure BGP or static routes for peering to Redwood's transit — confirm next-hop reachability and route advertisement windows.
   - NAT egress path: identify whether HealthMate will use shared NAT or dedicated egress.
   - MTU: if on-prem edge uses 9000, set instance NICs to 9000 and ensure LB/forwarders preserve jumbo frames.

2) Firewall & egress allowlist (we provided a csv attachment)
   - Ports: outbound TCP 443 (control plane), 5228-5230 (optional model-sync), 9411 (tracing), 123/UDP (optional NTP).
   - FQDNs: storage.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.net.

3) KMS & keys
   - Create a customer-managed KMS key with a Redwood service principal grantee.
   - Rotation policy: quarterly recommended; include RBAC for key perms.

4) Service accounts & IAM
   - Provide a dedicated service account for Redwood runtime with minimal scope (kms:Decrypt, storage:GetObject, logs:Write).
   - Support for short-lived STS tokens preferred — we'll provide an OIDC config if you can accept it.

5) Observability & logs
   - Syslog/forwarder endpoint or S3 bucket for audit logs.
   - Prometheus scrape endpoints are optional; we can provide exporters if direct scraping is blocked.

6) Validation runbook (our team will run this)
   - Step 1: TCP handshake to control-plane fqdn + certificate validation.
   - Step 2: PTR & forward DNS sanity for internal names.
   - Step 3: Model pull test (dry-run) and KV-cache warming.

I'll copy Dev and Marissa — they'll own the connectivity tests and the on-prem sizing guidance. Can your infra team share the CIDR plan and whether you'll require BGP?

Next steps:
- HealthMate to share CIDR plan & preferred NAT model by EOD Wed (6/30).
- Redwood to produce a refined checklist + KMS policy proposal by Thu (7/1).

PR: I've attached: hm-network-armature-v1.png, egress-ports-allowlist.csv.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: network-sanitation, access gating, and sprint action list

Looping in technical owners. A few quick notes from infra:
- MTU: we support jumbo frames end-to-end, but some cloud LBs strip them. If HealthMate's edge uses 9000, we need confirmation that intermediate forwarding preserves 9000. If not, we recommend 1500 to avoid fragmentation.
- BGP: we prefer BGP where available for automatic failover; static routes are OK for small POCs.
- IP plan: avoid overlap with Redwood default VPC ranges — we'll send our recommended host CIDR ranges.

Action items for Redwood:
- I'll produce a minimal nc/tcp test harness and a curl-based cert validation by Wed.
- Marissa will draft the KMS policy and minimal IAM perms.

Dev

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft KMS & IAM pattern + timeline

Sara — please see the attached KMS policy proposal (kms-policy-proposal.pdf). Key points:
- Redwood requests a dedicated key with a narrow IAM role that grants: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKeyOnly to the service principal.
- We will use envelope encryption; Redwood never stores plaintext.
- Rotation cadence: we recommend calendar-quarter rotation; HealthMate can opt-in for automatic rotation.

IAM/service account pattern:
- Create a service account (redwood-runtime@healthmate.io) and grant the role healthcare-redwood-runtime-viewer (contains the three KMS actions + storage read).
- For elevated ops (debug), create a separate role with temporary elevation via STS and record all use via audit logs.

Timeline proposal:
- 6/30: HealthMate sends CIDR plan + NAT decision (shared vs dedicated).
- 7/1: Redwood provides final checklist + KMS policy + egress csv (done).
- 7/2–7/6: HealthMate implements network changes in dev/stage and shares reachability reports.
- 7/7–7/9: Redwood runs connectivity & model-pull validation (we'll schedule a 2-hour window).

Attachments: kms-policy-proposal.pdf

Marissa
